title: Programming Stem Cells for Therapeutic Angiogenesis Using Biodegradable Polymeric Nanoparticles
protocol: Weigh out 3,523 mg of butanediol diacrylate (C).
Transfer the weighed butanediol diacrylate to a glass scintillation vial containing a stir bar.
Pre-heat 5-amino-1-pentanol (32) to 90 °C to solubilize the salt.
Weigh out 1,533 mg of pre-heated 5-amino-1-pentanol and add it to the scintillation vial containing C.
Place the vial onto a stir plate and set stir speed at 600 rpm.
Transfer the scintillation vial to an oven set at 90 °C.
Increase stirring speed to 1,000 rpm for 4 hr.
Lower the speed to 300 rpm after 4 hr and maintain at 90 °C for another 12-16 hr.
Weigh out 5 g of C32.
Add 5 g of C32 to 10 ml of anhydrous tetrahydrofuran (THF) in a glass scintillation vial containing a stir bar.
Wrap the vial with foil and vortex on high until fully dissolved.
In a separate glass scintillation vial containing a stir bar, add 10 mM of Tetraethyleneglycoldiamine (122).
Add 40 ml of THF to the vial containing 122.
Place both vials (C32 and 122) on a stir plate for 5 min then combine together.
Cover the combined vials in foil and leave at room temperature stirring at 400 rpm for 24 hr.
Weigh out 5 x 50 ml Falcon tubes for each 5 g batch of C32-122.
Note the mass of each tube in a notebook.
Transfer 30 ml of anhydrous diethyl ether to each 50 ml Falcon tube.
Transfer 10 ml of C32-122 to each 50 ml Falcon tube.
Vortex Falcon tubes vigorously.
Centrifuge Falcon tubes at 2,500 rpm for 2 min.
Discard the upper solution from the centrifuged tubes.
Repeat steps of vortexing and centrifuging two more times.
Place open tubes containing extracted C32-122 in a desiccator under vacuum overnight.
Weigh all tubes containing C32-122 to determine final mass of extracted polymer.
Dissolve extracted polymer in anhydrous DMSO at 100 mg/ml concentration.
Store dissolved polymer at -20°C protected from light and moisture.
Pre-coat base of T-150 tissue culture flask with 0.1% (wt/vol) gelatin.
Allow gelatin to remain in the flask for 30-45 min.
Aspirate gelatin from pre-coated T-150 flask.
Add 4 x 10^6 ADSCs (≤ passage 3) to the flask with 20 ml of DMEM containing 10% FBS, 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin and 10 ng/ml bFGF.
Place T-150 flask in incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight.
Dilute plasmid DNA (1 mg/ml) to a final concentration of 120 μg/ml in sodium acetate (25 mM) in a 15 ml Falcon tube.
Dilute C32-122 from 100 mg/ml to 3.6 mg/ml in sodium acetate (25 mM) in a second 15 ml Falcon tube.
Combine contents of each Falcon tube into a single 15 ml Falcon tube and vortex immediately for 10 seconds on high.
Let the combined solution sit at room temperature for 10 minutes to form nanoparticles.
Replace medium in tissue culture flask with 7.8 ml fully supplemented DMEM per 1.0 x 10^6 cells transfected while nanoparticle solution is forming.
Transfer nanoparticle solution to the tissue culture flask and tilt forward and backwards to spread evenly.
Place the tissue culture flask in an incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 4 hours.
Replace the nanoparticle containing media with DMEM after 2 hours of incubation.
Incubate further at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for another 2 hours before proceeding to in vivo injection.
Place the mouse under anesthesia with 1-3% dosage isoflurane by inhalation and oxygen flow rate of 1 L/min.
Remove hair from the abdominal region and both hindlimb areas of the mouse with shaving cream.
Make an incision at the center of the medial thigh towards the midline.
Cut through the overlying fat pad to expose the femoral artery.
Ligate the artery at two sites: distal (close to the knee) and proximal (just distal to the inguinal ligament).
Separate the artery from the vein.
Thread a 5-0 silk suture around the artery at each ligation site.
Tie off the artery with two knots to create the ligation.
Remove the artery between the two ligation points.
Wash the surgical area with PBS.
Suture the incision closed.
Anesthetize the mouse and keep it warm until re-awakening.
Inject 2-4 mg/kg Lidocaine subcutaneously at the incision site prior to re-awakening for pain management.
Subcutaneously deliver 0.05-0.1 mg/kg Buprenorphine at 12 and 24 hours post-operation.
Monitor the health status of mice daily for seven days by observing breathing pattern, overt pain or distress, and skin color.
Confirm hindlimb ischemia by laser Doppler perfusion imaging.
Wash transfected cells with PBS.
Trypsinize the cells.
Centrifuge the cells.
Count the cells.
Resuspend cells at a density of 10 x 10^6 cells per ml in PBS.
Separate cell suspensions into Eppendorf tubes at a volume of 110 μl for each mouse.
Place mice under anesthesia (2.5% isoflurane, 1 L/min oxygen flow rate).
Clean the injection site with alcohol wipes.
Utilize a 27 G tuberculin syringe to draw up and down into the syringe to ensure a homogeneous suspension is achieved.
Draw up 100 μl of the cell suspension volume into the syringe.
Inject half the cell suspension into the adductor muscle region.
Inject the other half of the cell suspension into the calf muscle region.
Leave the syringe in place for at least 15-30 seconds to prevent leakage of the cell suspension.
Remove the mouse from anesthesia and keep warm until it reawakens.
Clean the injection site with alcohol wipes.
Utilize an insulin syringe to load 100 μl of 15 mg/ml D-luciferin (the substrate for firefly luciferase).
Hold mice by the skin of their back to pull their anterior skin taut.
Insert needle intraperitoneally into the abdominal region and inject 100 μl of substrate.
Place the mouse in the IVIS luciferase imaging chamber under anesthesia.
Set parameters with an exposure time of 1.0 minute.
Begin acquiring images.
Mark the region of interest to measure the luciferase signal on the ischemic limb at the cell-injection site.
Continue measuring the luciferase signal every 3-5 minutes until it reaches a peak and begins to decline.
Remove mice from the chamber and anesthesia when complete.
Keep mice warm until they reawaken.
Shave areas overlying both hindlimbs and the abdominal region of the mouse cleanly.
Warm the mouse to 36 °C on a hot plate while monitoring body temperature by rectal thermometer.
Place the mouse on its dorsal surface with limbs exposed evenly on a non-reflective black surface.
Keep the mouse anesthetized by nose cone during imaging.
Position the laser Doppler sensor roughly 15 cm above the mouse, directing it towards the groin region.
Take images utilizing the LDPIwin software by pressing the Start button.
Euthanize the mouse by exposing it to 5% isoflurane for 3-5 minutes, then euthanizing the mouse by cervical dislocation.
Cut the skin surrounding the hindlimb circumferentially at the distal abdominal region and proximal to the hindlimb from ventral to dorsal surfaces.
Pull back the skin over the hindlimb to the foot.
Amputate the limb using blunt dissection scissors at the pelvic and femur joint.
Collect medial adductor muscles for analysis.
Embed one or both tissues in optimal cutting temperature (OCT) for cryosectioning if histology is required.
Submerge collected tissue samples into a bath of liquid nitrogen for at least 2 minutes for biochemical analysis.
Store samples at -80°C for future processing.
